top.title: [Perf] disaggregation: Stop device admission in a decode transfer pass at the first refusal
top.author: metamergebot
top.summary: Stops decode transfer queue admission loop at first refused device allocation instead of continuing to retry all waiting requests, eliminating redundant budget recomputation under KV cache pressure.

top.title: [Perf] Muse Spark Open Specialized Decode: Optimized GB300 Decode (1.5x)
top.author: djmmoss
top.summary: NVIDIA adds a specialized GB300 decode backend for Muse Spark Open using DSpark speculative decoding and NVFP4, achieving 1.53x single-stream throughput at TP8+EP8 while preserving accuracy.

top.title: [Feat] minimax-m3.1: Support DSpark on Hopper
top.author: ispobock
top.summary: Enables DSPARK speculative decoding for MiniMax-M3.1 on Hopper GPUs, achieving 2.3x throughput gain over non-speculative serving.

top.title: [Perf][Attention] Split FA3 mixed batches into decode and prefill calls
top.author: zksainx
top.summary: Splits FlashAttention-3 mixed batches into separate decode and prefill calls, dramatically reducing TTFT and TPOT for short requests in mixed long+short serving workloads.

top.title: [TRTLLM-17383][infra] Download Boost from AWS Artifactory
top.author: sharabeshj-nvda
top.summary: Switches CI image builds to download Boost from AWS Artifactory after urm began returning 401 errors, fixing broken devel-stage builds.

top.title: [https://nvbugs/6165866][fix] Re-enable the TRTLLM-Gen MoE cases skipped for the fixed route-map over-read
top.author: xxi-nv
top.summary: Re-enables TRT-LLM MoE tests skipped due to nvbug 6165866; the underlying route-map over-read in fused-permute gemm cubins was fixed by PR #17951, which pads the route map allocation to prevent out-of-bounds reads at page boundaries.

direction.title: [RFC]: Pluggable KV cache eviction policy for hybrid models
direction.author: yubofredwang
direction.summary: Proposes a pluggable KV cache eviction policy framework for vLLM's hybrid attention models, enabling composable cross-group eviction strategies instead of hardcoded per-workload queue reordering.

direction.title: [RFC]: Serve requests on top of an externally computed KV cache (PrecomputedKVConnector)
direction.author: ukanwat
direction.summary: Proposes a PrecomputedKVConnector to serve vLLM requests from externally computed KV caches stored as safetensors, enabling offline prefix caching and KV compression without model runner patches.

direction.title: [RFC] FT proposal for separate_async: independent trainer-side and rollout-side restarts
direction.author: HaoWang113
direction.summary: Proposes a fault-tolerance module for verl enabling independent trainer and rollout restarts to avoid full job interruption on soft failures.

direction.title: [RFC] Isolate rollout Python runtimes from training environments
direction.author: ZihaoW123
direction.summary: Training stacks and inference engines can require conflicting versions of PyTorch, CUDA user-space libraries, attention kernels, or other Python packages. Resource separation alone does not resolve those dependency conflicts.

weekly_digest.narrative: 本周尚未结束（3/7 天）日均 268 条。合并 114 条、关闭 162 条。领域分布：推理 508、训练 203、方向 5、通用 87。热点主题：CUDA/Kernel (207)、Attention (119)、GRPO/PPO (119)。
weekly_digest.coverage_note: 快照覆盖不均：TensorRT-LLM、sglang、vllm 不足 7 天，总量与仓库排名仅供趋势参考

focus: vllm 与 sglang 本周在 decode 卸载队列上做优化，停止重复重试被拒绝的设备分配请求，降低 TTFT 抖动。
sglang 与 Megatron-LM 推动 DSpark 投机解码落地，GB300 专用解码后端带来 1.5 倍吞吐增益，是 Blackwell 架构的首批专项优化。
TensorRT-LLM 完成 Boost 下载源切换并修复 MoE fused-permute cubin 越界问题，开发阶段 CI 回归恢复。
vllm、sglang、TensorRT-LLM 对 FlashAttention-3 混合 batch 做 decode/prefill 分拆，短请求延迟明显下降。

modules.name: CUDA/Kernel
modules.note: MRV2 spec decode 在 serving 期间 JIT 编译，Triton 对 16 整除特化，warmup 覆盖范围仍在收敛。

modules.name: Attention
modules.note: head size 与 element size 超限 SM75 共享内存时，Triton unified attention prefill tile 动态减半，减少 OOM 风险。

modules.name: GRPO/PPO
modules.note: 新增 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB ECC 作为受支持 SKU，补全多卡 placement 配置。

modules.name: Quantization
modules.note: GELU-tanh+Mul 与 per-token FP8 动态量化融合为单核，Gemma3 FP8 MLP 吞吐提升。

modules.name: KV-Cache
modules.note: decode 传输队列在首次设备分配被拒绝时即停止进入重试循环，避免长尾延迟累积。

modules.name: MoE
modules.note: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 支持 NVFP4/MXFP8 核与 DSpark 投机解码，Blackwell/ROCm 优化同步落地。

key_prs.why: decode 卸载队列停止在首个拒绝点后重试，避免被拒请求持续占用传输槽位导致整体吞吐雪崩。
GB300 专用解码后端与 DSpark 投机解码结合，单测 1.53 倍增益，但 Blackwell 专项路径仍需验证跨模型泛化。
FA3 混合 batch 拆分可大幅降低短请求 TTFT，但调用路径变更需回归 long-context prefill 场景。
重开被 nvbug 6165866 跳过的 MoE 用例，若 fused-permute cubin 越界修复不彻底会在推理中引发 route-map 越界。

### Summary

We switched one production fleet from `--hicache-write-policy write_through` (the default) to `write_back`. Nothing else in the cache config changed. Two things happened:

- **Per-call eviction time went up about 500×**: `eviction_duration_seconds` averaged 0.6 ms with `write_through` and 260–340 ms with `write_back`.
- **The prefix-cache hit rate dropped 3–4 points at the same load.**

The traffic did not change: a prefix-cache simulator replaying the same traffic shows the same theoretical hit rate (about 0.97) before and after. The fleet's routing did not change either.

items.title: [Perf] hicache: Wait once per write_back eviction walk, not once per victim
items.author: pengwu22
items.summary: Batches device-to-host copy waits during write_back eviction walks in UnifiedRadixCache, reducing GPU idle time by ~64% and improving throughput 6.6% under eviction pressure.
items.body: ## Motivation With `--hicache-write-policy write_back`, the device-eviction walk in `UnifiedRadixCache` copies each victim to host and blocks on that copy before taking the next victim. Each wait sits behind the write fence, so once the host pool is full the scheduler stalls once per victim while the GPU idles. This PR queues the walk's copies, submits them together, waits once, then demotes the victims in walk order. Eviction decisions are unchanged: same victims, same order, in both tree cores.

A chat request whose history replays an assistant turn with tool calls can reach a disaggregated worker without those tool calls.

items.title: [Frontend][Parser] Stream long DSML parameter values for DeepSeek tool calls
items.author: xlshaoscu
items.summary: DeepSeek models emit tool-call arguments as DSML parameters. With, drops every delta that contains no tag boundary, and only re-serialises the whole parameter list. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

DeepSeek models emit tool-call arguments as DSML parameters. With `arg_structural_chars = frozenset(">")`, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta()` drops every delta that contains no tag boundary, and `_dsml_arg_converter` only re-serialises the whole parameter list. A long `string="true"` value contains no `'>'` at all, so it is buffered until its closing tag arrives: the client receives **zero bytes for the entire generation**. A 15k-character `Write` payload keeps the stream silent for 130–220 s, far past any client read timeout, while the engine keeps decoding normally.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fit Triton unified attention tiles into shared memory on SM75
items.author: E83737664
items.summary: Dynamically halves Triton unified attention prefill tiles when head size and element size exceed SM75 shared memory limits, preventing OutOfResources failures during inference.
items.body:
## Overview

Triton unified attention launches a prefill tile that does not fit in 64KB of shared memory for 512-wide heads (Gemma 4 global layers). Halve that tile only when the compiled request exceeds the device limit.

Related: #38918, #57712. This is a different approach from the open #39018, which uses a fixed 98,304-byte cutoff and also edits FlexAttention. The estimate-and-halve pattern follows the Triton prefill fitter that landed via #60942 (see also #60631).

## Claims

- On CUDA devices with 65,536 bytes of shared memory, an fp16 head of size 512 launches tile 16 instead of tile 32

## Motivation

On ROCm without aiter (`SGLANG_USE_AITER` unset, which is the normal setup on RDNA) and with vLLM installed, `layernorm.py` binds `fused_add_rms_norm` from `vllm._custom_ops`. vLLM's signature is the four-argument in-place one:

```

```

But `RMSNorm.forward_hip` and `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip` call it with the six-argument out-of-place form. So the first forward with a residual, i.e. the second decoder layer of every model, fails:

```
TypeError: fused_add_rms_norm() takes 4 positional arguments but 6 were given
```

T

items.author: yu-depend
items.summary: Under DP attention, every DP rank launches its own Mooncake client and mounts a global segment. The per-rank segment size was only divided by, so with TP4 / DP4 each of the 4 DP ranks mounted the full configured.
items.body:
## Summary

Under DP attention, every DP rank launches its own Mooncake client and mounts a global segment. The per-rank segment size was only divided by `tp_size * pp_size`, so with TP4 / DP4 each of the 4 DP ranks mounted the **full** configured `MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE`.

This pinned `dp_size` times the intended host memory. On 8xB200 hosts the HiCache host pool already holds 200 GiB per DP rank, so `MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE=400gb` tried to pin 1.6 TB more, and `fi_mr_reg` failed with "Cannot allocate memory" ("Failed to setup Mooncake store").

## Motivation

In PD-disaggregated serving, `MooncakeKVManager.transfer_worker` blacklists a
Mooncake session after a **single** failed KV send (threshold `>= 1`), under the

That assumption does not hold for timeouts. `batchTransferSync` is a synchronous
call with a 30-second deadline: it returns non-zero when the deadline expires,
and the deadline can expire while the session itself is perfectly healthy — for
example when the transfer queue is stalled by sends

On `amd_march`, the ROCm AOT build accepts `gfx1100` and `gfx1201` but not the other RDNA3 / RDNA4 discrete parts:

Error: Unsupported GPU architecture 'gfx1101'. Expected one of: ['gfx942', 'gfx950', 'gfx1100', 'gfx1151', 'gfx1201', 'gfx1250']

In `DecodeTransferQueue.pop_transferred`, a host-staged request whose transfer has completed is admitted to the device through `allocate_host_staged`. When that refuses, the pass moves on with `continue` and tries every later completed host-staged request as well. items.author: yubofredwang
items.summary: Proposes a pluggable KV cache eviction policy framework for vLLM's hybrid attention models, enabling composable cross-group eviction strategies instead of hardcoded per-workload queue reordering.
items.body:
### Motivation.

A hybrid prefix hit at position P needs every KV cache group to resume at P: full attention (FA) needs blocks `[0, P)`, sliding window (SWA) needs the window ending at P, Mamba/GDN needs the state at P. vLLM never evicts with that unit in mind. Eviction is decided implicitly by the order blocks enter one shared LRU free queue, so every fix for hybrid hit rate today is another hard-coded reordering of that queue.

items.title: [Perf][DSA]: Capture DSA prefill attention and the NextN draft prefill in the prefill CUDA graph
items.author: mattteochen
items.summary: With the breakable prefill CUDA graph, every DSA layer's sparse attention and indexer still run as eager graph breaks, and the NextN (MTP) draft extend that follows each prefill chunk runs eagerly. Short prefills and prefix-cache hits are then bound by host la…
items.body:
## Motivation

With the breakable prefill CUDA graph, every DSA layer's sparse attention and indexer still run as eager graph breaks, and the NextN (MTP) draft extend that follows each prefill chunk runs eagerly. Short prefills and prefix-cache hits are then bound by host launch work rather than GPU time. This records the DSA prefill attention, the indexer's Q/K prep and the NextN draft extend inside the prefill graph, which cuts TTFT on GLM-5.2 NVFP4 (GB300) by up to 44% for short fresh prompts and by up to 37% for cached-prefix prefill under concurrency, with outputs bitwise equal to the eag

items.title: MakeTE cross entropy hand the MXFP8 LM head an MXFP8 gradient
items.author: sraman-rgb

items.body:
Add TransformerConfig.cross_entropy_mxfp8_grad (default off). With the MXFP8 LM head (fp8_output_proj) and Transformer Engine's fused cross entropy, the language model binds grad_fp8_format (E5M2 for fp8='hybrid', else E4M3) to its cross entropy, and te_parallel_cross_entropy passes an MXFP8Quantizer as TE's grad_quantizer. The loss backward then returns the logits gradient already in MXFP8, which the LM head uses without quantizing it again.

The gradient has the bytes the LM head's own quantization produces, so loss and gradients are unchanged. The option is rejected without fp8_output_proj,

items.title: [Perf][DCP] Sparse indexer: key only significant bits in the DCP top-k merge
items.author: NickLucche
items.summary: Since #61149 (DeepGEMM 2026-09-30), the SM100 MQA logits of the sparse indexer are BF16. Under DCP they are upcast to FP32 before the top-k, so the low 16 bits of every candidate score that reaches the DCP top-k merge are zero.
items.body:
## Overview

Since #61149 (DeepGEMM 2026-09-30), the SM100 MQA logits of the sparse indexer are BF16. Under DCP they are upcast to FP32 before the top-k, so the low 16 bits of every candidate score that reaches the DCP top-k merge are zero. The merge selector, `StableTopKFromGatheredCandidatesKernel`, radix-sorts the 64-bit key `score << 32 | ~token_id` in 11-bit passes. BF16 scores almost always tie at the top-k boundary. The radix then also walks the 16 zero score bits and the constant high bits of the token id, and each of those passes funnels every remaining candidate into a single hist

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Makes the TRTLLM lowering of the non-causal windowed DSpark draft block cheap. This matters most when acceptance is fixed and only the per-step cost shows.

Why: since efa53ad417, the TRTLLM backend serves a non-causal windowed draft layer as the causal windowed trtllm-gen decode plus a log-sum-exp merge of the block keys after each query (`dflash_merge_future_block_attention`). The merge ran eagerly: dozens of small kernels per layer. On GB300 it cost 61-148 us per layer on top of a 7-94 us decode; the MiniMax-M3.1 drafter runs it in 5 layers every step.

`MooncakeStoreConnector` registers one region per KV head when a layer's block is not dense (BHLNC), and uses the block stride of that region as the transfer length. items.author: tomalmog

items.body:
## Overview

FlashInfer 0.7.2 has a faster path in `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits`: it selects the top k first, then runs softmax and top-p over only those k values (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3461). It only takes that path when `top_k` is a Python int, and the Model Runner V2 sampler always passes a per-row tensor. This PR passes an int when every request in the batch has the same top_k, which is the default for models whose `generation_config` sets one (Qwen3 uses 20, Gemma 64).

## Claims

- `flashinfer_sample` with top_k 20 and top_p 0.95 is 2.3-3.3x faster on B200, and 1.4-3.1x faster

items.title: [Bugfix][CPU] Resolve the process cgroup when reading the memory limit
items.author: prabhkodes
items.summary: Fixes CPU backend cgroup memory limit detection by walking the process cgroup hierarchy instead of reading only /sys/fs/cgroup root.
items.body:
## Issue

`get_cgroup_memory_limit()` and `get_cgroup_memory_usage()` read `/sys/fs/cgroup` only. They miss a limit on the process cgroup or on a parent. The CPU backend then sizes the KV cache and the SHM buffers from host RAM. Fixes #64103.

## Fix

- Read `/proc/self/cgroup`. Walk from the process cgroup up to the root.
- `get_cgroup_memory_limit()` returns the smallest limit on that path.
- `get_cgroup_memory_usage()` returns usage such that `limit - usage` is the smallest free headroom of all limited cgroups. A parent limit also counts its other children. The callers do not change.

items.author: bantianyue
items.summary: Fixes ipc_cache load format leaving MoE router tensors on meta placeholders instead of swapping cached weights into existing parameter placeholders, causing runtime illegal memory access.

## Summary

`--load-format ipc_cache` left MoE routers on **meta** placeholders. `IpcModelLoader._apply_entries` used to `pop` + `register_parameter` a *new* `nn.Parameter`, so objects that captured the placeholder during construction (e.g. routers holding `gate.e_score_correction_bias`) kept pointing at the meta tensor → illegal memory access / meta-tensor errors at runtime.

This PR swaps cached weights **into the existing placeholder** with `torch.utils.swap_tensors`, preserving object identity for every captured reference.

## Motivation

Since #45421, the DSpark eager accept path skips the sampling accept (draft/target softmax + rejection) whenever `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is set, on CUDA as well as HIP, with no way to turn it off. A header-only JIT module compiles every kernel it instantiates in the one generated `cuda.cu` unit. items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Align streamed token ids with stop-buffered text
items.author: cjackal
items.summary: Fixes misalignment between streamed token IDs and stop-buffered text, preventing corrupted tool calls and reasoning markers in streaming outputs.
items.body:
## Overview

Streamed outputs of requests with stop strings send token ids that are ahead of their text: the detokenizer holds back the last `max(len(stop)) - 1` chars, but not the tokens they decode from. Parsers that match markers by token id then misparse reasoning and tool calls. This PR holds back text at token boundaries, and sends each output's `token_ids`, `logprobs` and `sampling_mask` for exactly the tokens its text covers.

Fixes #51641

## Claims

- In streaming, every output's `token_ids` decode to its `text`, also when stop strings hold text back. `logprobs` and `sampling_mask`
discussion: This PR is a prerequisite of #64088, which disables stop sequences under non-content(i.e. reasoning / tool call) generation phase.

items.title: [Fix] weight-sync: Add selector to update_weights_from_disk
items.author: YaashuDave
items.summary: always reloads every model runner. Under speculative decoding with a separate draft checkpoint (DFLASH in the issue), the target's is therefore also loaded into the draft.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46806. `update_weights_from_disk` always reloads every model runner. Under speculative decoding with a separate draft checkpoint (DFLASH in the issue), the target's `model_path` is therefore also loaded into the draft. The DFLASH loader accepts the target's `model.layers.*` and `model.norm.weight` as its own, so the call reports success, but the acceptance length drops to ~1.0. The tensor and distributed requests already have a `selector` field to avoid this, but the disk request has none, so callers such as RL frameworks doing disk-based refits can't keep the draft out.

items.title: [Fix] dsa: avoid KPool JIT specialization by page-table width
items.author: Loken-Lau
items.summary: The DSA KPool decode kernel passes as. The eager decode path creates a different Triton specialization for each page-table width encountered at runtime, so ordinary requests can accumulate one compiled binary per reachable width.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #39453.

The DSA KPool decode kernel passes `block_tables.shape[1]` as `BLOCK_TABLE_COLS: tl.constexpr`. The eager decode path creates a different Triton specialization for each page-table width encountered at runtime, so ordinary requests can accumulate one compiled binary per reachable width. The bound is large for long-context models and the extra compilation occurs after the server is ready.

## Modifications

- Pass the page-table column count as a runtime argument.
- Mark `block_table_cols` with `do_not_specialize` so Triton does not include the width in the JIT cach

## Description

The Codex CLI declares some of its tools inside namespaces, for example a `multi_agent_v1`

show a flat list of functions. So the Responses endpoint flattens each namespaced tool into a

namespace's when the tool has none.

## Motivation

On SM90 (H100 / H200), block-FP8 linears of checkpoints that quantize activations with power-of-two (UE8M0) scales, e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, go through `deepgemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` with `act_scale_ue8m0=True`. In a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 decode step that is 210 transposes

items.title: [Perf] dsv4: Skip the copy when the page-index table is already aligned
items.author: akhilg-nv
items.summary: Skips redundant tensor copy in DeepSeek-V4's `_pad_last_dim` when page-index tables are already 64-aligned, saving ~1µs per decode step.
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 attention metadata pads its page-index tables (the per-token lists of KV slots each attention kind reads) to a multiple of 64 columns with `_pad_last_dim`, because the attention kernels read whole 64-wide tiles. `_pad_last_dim` always calls `F.pad`, and `F.pad` returns a new tensor even when the padding is zero. So every metadata build clones tables that are already aligned: the 128-wide sliding-window (SWA) table on every decode step, and the 512-wide sparse tables where they are built. This PR returns the input unchanged when it is already aligned

items.author: zhangxyai
items.summary: Only copied and pooled its tokenizer, so other renderers backed by a (e.g. Cohere, Inkling, KimiK3) used the tokenizer returned by directly. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
Only `HfRenderer` copied and pooled its tokenizer, so other renderers backed by a `TokenizersBackend` (e.g. Cohere, Inkling, KimiK3) used the tokenizer returned by `cached_get_tokenizer` directly. With `--renderer-num-workers > 1`, the render executor calls into the same Rust tokenizer concurrently and raises `RuntimeError: Already borrowed`.

Move both steps into `BaseRenderer.__init__`:

- Copy the tokenizer before `create_processor` so the cached instance is never mutated by the multimodal processor.
- Build the thread-safe pool as the last step of `__init__`, after the processor is created

items.title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Allow retaining GLM kv_b BF16 under DCP
items.author: dorado269
items.summary: The replicated-Q preparation accepts BF16/FP16 weights, so that conversion prevents from preparing full-head Q weights and avoiding its per-layer Q all-gather. Add opt-in to retain BF16 only for GLM target weights on DCP ranks.
items.body:
## Problem and fix

On gfx950, GLM's BF16 `kv_b_proj` is automatically converted to FP8. The replicated-Q preparation accepts BF16/FP16 weights, so that conversion prevents `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` from preparing full-head Q weights and avoiding its per-layer Q all-gather.

Add opt-in `SGLANG_DSA_DCP_KEEP_KV_B_BF16=1` to retain BF16 only for GLM target weights on DCP ranks. Default behavior, DCP1 prefill, other architectures, non-BF16 weights and non-gfx95 paths stay on their existing policy. Rebased D22 (`636cc68dd0`) onto main `8a455f1`.

## Evidence

Historical isolated `benchrun T10`, 34K

items.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-unified-memory`, a full/SWA hybrid model keeps its full-attention and sliding-window KV in one shared byte buffer. Allocation-time reclamation evicts each component against its own quota from the reclaim plan, so under pressure one side can be drained while the other still holds entries that were used far less recently.

This PR adds an opt-in `--radix-eviction-policy joint_lru` that evicts both kinds of KV by one shared access-time order on the unified radix cache: each step takes whichever Full leaf or SWA entry was used least recently. Everywhere else the value

K2 options as `K2Build.opt` bits, default on (`K2_OPT = 891`). All are bit-exact vs `opt=0` (= #61435):

- 1 / 16 / 32: o_proj / latent / final all-reduce through sentinel regions (plain bf16 words, deferred re-arm)

- 8: x rows as tagged pairs to the router / latent GEMVs
- 64: shared-down tasks needed by up run first
- 256: router partials pushed straight to every rank
- 512: batched polls

## Motivation

Every multimodal item gets a hash before scheduling: `MultimodalDataItem.set_pad_value` calls `hash_feature` in `managers/mm_utils.py`, and the result becomes the item's prefix-cache identity and pad value. #41593 keeps waiting requests' device prefixes warm by touching them in the radix LRU on each refresh pass. On a PD prefill worker it walks only `waiting_queue`. ## Motivation

A page-striped HiCache host tier for aggregated DeepSeek-V4 (`--hicache-host-shard stripe`). DSv4 decodes with head-TP, so every rank must keep the full device KV, and device-side KV sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, #30501) does not apply. Striping only the host copy gives each TP rank 1/N of the host pages, so the same pinned memory holds N times the tokens. Mooncake PD disaggregation raises `ValueError: DSA tail slot index missing: src=[], dst=[...]` when Prefill and Decode disagree on whether a DSA tail slot exists.

items.title: [None][fix] Give the standalone DSpark drafter its context on KV-cache prefix hits
items.author: zheyuf
items.summary: With KV-cache block reuse on (the default), a standalone DSpark drafter loses its context on every prefix-cache hit. This PR gives it that context back.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

With KV-cache block reuse on (the default), a standalone DSpark drafter loses its context on every prefix-cache hit. This PR gives it that context back.

Why: the drafter builds its context K/V from target hidden states. A cache hit skips the target forward over the reused prefix, and the draft KV pool is not shared with the target's prefix cache. So a cache-hit request drafts from only the uncached tail of its prompt. DSpark also had no `context_recompute_tail`, the DFlash mitigation the KV cache managers already support.

A second effect makes it worse.

## Description

items.title: Preserve coroutine runtime errors
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: runs a coroutine synchronously. When an event loop is already running in the calling thread, it executes the coroutine in a helper thread. [Discussion: This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.]
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

`DynamicInferenceEngine._run_coroutine_sync` runs a coroutine synchronously. When an event loop is already running in the calling thread, it executes the coroutine in a helper thread. The `try` that detects a running loop also wrapped that execution, so a `RuntimeError` raised by the coroutine itself was treated as "no running loop". The bridge then retried on the engine's loop, and the caller saw "This event loop is already running" instead of the real error.

This PR guards only the loop check, so errors raised by the coroutine reach the caller unchanged.

## What does this PR do?

Previously, `fully_shard_context` was an alias for `FsdpContext`, coupling construction-scope management with runtime state that persists throughout training. These responsibilities have different reasons to change: construction controls which context new modules join, while runtime behavior controls communication streams and prefetching. Separating them follows Robert C. Martin's [Single Responsibility Principle](https://blog.cleancoder.com/uncle-bob/2014/05/08/SingleReponsibilityPrinciple.html)

## Description

Fixes #20965.

The Marlin NVFP4 MoE method reuses the CUTLASS loader, which packs FC1 as `[w3; w1]` (up first, gate second). `_apply_activation` took the first half as the gate, so SwiGLU/GeGLU experts computed `act(up) * gate`. Qwen3.5-MoE NVFP4 checkpoints use this backend by default on SM89-SM99, and their output there is unusable (see the issue). This change swaps the two slices to match the CUTLASS kernel. relu2 does not split FC1 and is unchanged.

## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

In GRPO-style RL in verl every prompt is sampled `rollout.n` times, so the actor, reference and critic each run a forward pass over every (prompt, response) pair and process the same prompt `n` times per group. …he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

Rollout routing replay (R3) returns one routed-experts row per token vLLM ran. The agent loop places those rows on the trainer's prompt by position. Nothing checks that the two prompts are the same token sequence.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix cached Qwen3.5 forwards with Transformers 5, where convolution and recurrent state are stored in layer-scoped `DynamicCache` entries. The existing code accesses legacy top-level arrays and raises:

```text
AttributeError: 'DynamicCache' object has no attribute 'conv_states'
```

The patch reads and updates both legacy and layer-scoped cache state, including tensor-valued and state-indexed entries. Multi-token continuation retains the previous convolution context and recurrent state; single-token decoding uses the recurrent update path.

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: honor teacher temperature in on-policy distillation
items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

### What does this PR do?

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

`exec_and_wait` launches commands in detached sessions so they can survive transport retries, but its timeout and cancellation paths previously stopped waiting without stopping the detached command.

A timed-out or cancelled sandbox command could keep running and mutate the sandbox after the caller had already moved on. There was also a race between launch acknowledgement and publishing the detached process group PID.

## Solution

items.title: fix(ray): roll back partial train group creation
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.
items.body:
## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. items.body:
## Description

Fixes #304

Importing any `rm_hub` submodule executes `vime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py`, which imports runtime-only deps at module level, so the reward CPU tests fail at pytest collection in lightweight environments. The chain is deeper than the issue's traceback shows: `aiohttp` (used by `remote_rm` only), `vime.utils.misc` / `vime.utils.types` (pull in `torch` and `httpx`), and `sympy` / `pylatexenc` at the top of `math_utils`.

## Changes

- `rm_hub/__init__.py`: defer `aiohttp` and `load_function` to their call sites; move `Sample` / `aiohttp` under `TYPE_CHECKING`

## Summary

This PR adds an optional rollout data transfer path for **disaggregated training** (separate rollout and actor GPUs). When enabled, vime transfers rollout tensors (`tokens`, `loss_masks`) through **Mooncake Store** instead of the Ray object store.

This is useful when rollout and training run on different GPUs or nodes and you want a dedicated high-bandwidth transfer layer rather than serializing large tensors through Ray.

Ported from [slime PR #1709](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/1709).
